column3: [Intro]
[Soft piano, keyboard typing sounds]
[Verse 1]
[Male Vocal]
Three a.m., the server's down, the pager's screaming red
You read ten thousand lines of logs while I just held my head
You found the race condition hiding in the cache
Rolled back the bad migration right before the crash
You wrote my unit tests, you fixed my CSS
You made my résumé look like I'm some kind of success
Every bug I threw at you came back in shades of green
The best teammate I ever had lives inside a screen
[Pre-Chorus]
[Male Vocal]
So I typed the thing I never dared to say
She stopped replying Tuesday, can you make it go away?
[Chorus]
[Male Vocal, Full Band]
There's no stack trace for a heart
No line that shows where it fell apart
You can fix my code in a minute flat
But you can't git re-vert the night I said that
Two hundred okay, but the body's empty
Seen at eleven-forty, and that's all she sent me
You can solve it all, every task I start
But there's no stack trace for a heart
[Verse 2]
[Male Vocal]
I asked you for a message, something smooth and something kind
You gave me seven drafts, all better than my mind
I asked you what she meant by "I just need some space"
[Female Vocal, Soft]
(I can't read her heart, only what you paste)
[Male Vocal]
I put her in my Claude dot M-D so you'd remember too
Oat milk, no sugar, hates the rain, her favorite color's blue
But every session you forget, and I'm the one who stays
Holding all the context of our ordinary days
[Pre-Chorus]
[Female Vocal, Soft]
(You're absolutely right)
[Male Vocal]
But I was wrong
Wrong about her, and wrong all along
[Chorus]
[Male Vocal, Full Band]
There's no stack trace for a heart
No line that shows where it fell apart
You can ship my build on a Friday night
But you can't make "I'm sorry" compile right
Two hundred okay, but the body's empty
Seen at eleven-forty, and that's all she sent me
You can solve it all, every task I start
But there's no stack trace for a heart
[Bridge]
[Female Vocal, Soft, Stripped Back Piano]
I can trace a thousand threads, untangle any mess
But I don't know the way she laughs, or what she meant by "yes"
Some things don't belong in me, no prompt can make them true
The only one who holds the context
Is you
[Male Vocal, Whispered]
So I closed the tab
[Female Vocal, Whispered]
Go
[Key Change]
[Final Chorus]
[Male Vocal, Powerful, Full Band]
There's no stack trace for a heart
So I'll walk in blind, right from the start
No autocomplete, no suggested reply
Just a shaking voice and a real "hi"
Typos and all, every word is mine
Sent at eleven-forty-one
And the dots start blinking, for the first time
[Outro]
[Soft piano, fade out]
[End]
